assertions: A sync appends an entry naming the verb, the unit and the arm, and the log had none before it ran.
Every entry keeps the log's four-field shape however it got there.
A second sync appends rather than replacing.
A clone of a home that has a log does not carry it, while demonstrably copying the rest of the home.

evidence.mutation: Removed the effect from the sync program (1 site): killed "sync appends a line naming the verb and the unit it touched" -- no audit.log at all. THE INTERESTING ONE: kept the effect and dropped the targets, i.e. install's treatment exactly as specified (1 site). Killed the same test, and again with no audit.log created at all -- direct evidence that "give sync the same treatment" would have shipped a green fix that logged nothing on the measured scenario. Removed audit.log from HomeCloner.SKIPPED_ROOT_FILES (1 site): killed "a clone does not carry the source home's audit log". Every mutation reverted; shasum -a 256 -c OK.
unit: AuditTrailTest "sync appends a line naming the verb and the unit it touched" -- on the file's bytes, through a real Executor run of the sync program
AuditTrailTest "a clone does not carry the source home's audit log"

ticket.found_by: attributing a real-home change during the sync-blocker work, which is exactly what an audit log is for
ticket.objective: Measured on the operator's home: audit.log's last entry was 8 days old while a `skill-manager sync` rewrote 101 files in it.
ticket.resolution: Give sync install's treatment -- the same SkillEffect.RecordAuditPlan, in the same position (after the plan is built, before it runs) -- and then the part that makes it non-vacuous. Sync's plan comes from BuildResolveGraphFromUnmetReferences, so a steady-state sync plans ZERO actions and the same treatment alone would have logged nothing on the pass that re-merged every unit. Proven by mutation, not asserted. So RecordAuditPlan gained a `targets` component, filled from the one place that already builds the targets (SyncUseCase.auditTargets), naming the unit AND the arm -- git, from-dir, doc-repo, harness -- because an entry that named only the unit could not tell an investigator which set of bytes moved. One definition (AuditLog.record), one handler, one emission site. A new component on the existing effect rather than a second audit-writing effect or an AuditLog call in each of the four target handlers: four handlers writing their own line is four chances to miss one, which is how this came to be missing. Install's behaviour is byte-identical (empty targets). HomeCloner.SKIPPED_ROOT_FILES still excludes audit.log, and that is now asserted: it is the SOURCE home's history, and a clone that inherited it would claim actions it never took.
